newsitem.title: UK: UK sees drop in wool producers, sheep numbers.
newsitem.headline: UK sees drop in wool producers, sheep numbers.

text.p: The number of wool producers in the UK fell by around four percent to 85,900 during 1996, according to figures issued by the British Wool Marketing Board.
"It's at the lowest level since at least 1950," press officer Liz Ambler said.
Industry sources said the decline was due to farm closures and mergers, part of a rationalisation in the sheepfarming sector that has been taking place for the past four years.
Sheep numbers have also dropped, dipping below 43 million after reaching the decade's peak of 44 million in 1993 and flopping to 43.295 million in 1994.
Ambler said clip weights have been on an upward trend as a result of changes in farming practice and are likely to counterbalance the reduced headcount.
However, the average clip weight for 1996 is not expected to reach 1995's record high of 706 kgs.
Official figures for the size of the 1996 clip will be available by the beginning of February.
